message.content:
To force‑close Visual Studio Code from the command line on Windows you can use **`taskkill`** against the executable that VS Code runs – `code.exe`.

```cmd
:: Kill all running instances of VS Code (forceful)
taskkill /IM code.exe /F

:: If you also want to make sure any child processes started by VS Code are terminated:
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

### What each switch does

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Specify the image name (process name). In this case `code.exe`. |
| `/F`   | Forcefully terminate the process(es). |
| `/T`   | Terminate the specified process and any child processes it has spawned. |

> **Tip:**  
> If you’re unsure whether `code.exe` is the correct process name on your machine, run `tasklist | findstr code.exe` first to confirm.

### Running from PowerShell

If you prefer PowerShell, you can do the same thing with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to include child processes:

```powershell
Get-Process code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
```

---

**Caution:** Using `/F` will terminate the process immediately without giving VS Code a chance to clean up. Make sure you’ve saved all work before running this command.
